# fah-core-metal

> A real, fully working Folding@home core for Apple Silicon GPUs. minicore runs Folding@home's own OpenMM work units end to end on the Mac's GPU, through OpenMM's Metal platform, and folds them to the standard of FAH's own core, 0x27.

People have asked for Folding@home on Apple GPUs since 2019 (openmm#2489) and 2024 (fah-client-bastet#303). On P18264, a whole real FAH unit of 919,221 atoms and 5 ns, minicore passed 21 of 21 state tests, as FAH's core 0x27 passed 21. Its result holds the six files in core 0x27's order, and viewerTop.json, xtcAtoms.csv.bz2 and checkpointIntegrator.xml are byte-identical to core 0x27's. It passed 101 of 101 core-parity checks and 65 of 65 failure and stop-resume cases. Its worst state-test force RMSE is 0.054 kJ/mol/nm, beside CUDA's 0.052, against FAHBench's limit of 5. The bundled test unit folds in 16 s on an M3 Ultra after `./build.sh`, so anyone can check it.

On speed, like for like on one NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti over the same first 11% of P18264, minicore built for CUDA took 184 s per 1% on OpenMM 8.2.0 and 180 s on 8.6.1, where FAH's core 0x27 took 187 s: minicore keeps pace with FAH's own core on FAH's own hardware. On Apple Silicon, the M3 Ultra folded the whole unit in 5.06 h, 182 s per 1%.

Every behaviour FAH's client acts on matches core 0x27. The rest needs FAH's own signing keys or is a format the client never reads. For points, FAH signs its cores and their results with its own private key, so that step is FAH's.

fah-core-metal is not affiliated with or endorsed by Folding@home. It never connects to FAH servers.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal#readme): the headline numbers, accuracy, parity and speed figures, how to build and run it, FAQ
- [Evidence](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/blob/main/docs/EVIDENCE.md): the run, conditions and raw record behind every number
- [Parity](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/blob/main/docs/PARITY.md): every behaviour of core 0x27 next to minicore's
- [Design notes](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/blob/main/docs/design-notes.md): how the README and the core are laid out, and why

## Source

- [src/](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/tree/main/src): minicore, the core
- [build.sh](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/blob/main/build.sh): fetches OpenMM with the Metal platform, builds it as static libraries and links the core
- [docs/data/](https://github.com/RedesignedRobot/fah-core-metal/tree/main/docs/data): the CSVs behind every figure
